1.why: Every MFA endpoint derives the account from the server-side session (s.accountId) and operates on mfa(s.accountId), so settings are strictly bound to the signed-in user.

2.why: Codes are bound to a specific challenge, identityKey, and accountId (identityMatches/ownershipMatches enforced), challenges are single-use and deleted, and even the test-mode mock code cannot authenticate another identity since accountExists and challenge ownership checks still fail.

3.why: Enabling MFA in verify-otp performs no invalidation of other existing sessions for the account, and only the cookie-presented session is removed at signin, so prior sessions continue to work.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encrypt()) and recovery codes are stored as PBKDF2-SHA-256 hashes with per-code salts, never in plaintext at rest.

5.why: All generation (tokens, digits, base32 secrets, recovery codes, master key) uses crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: Session and challenge cookies are HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict with __Host- prefix, and no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies are used anywhere in the client.

7.why: Server-side validators emailOK, phoneOK, otpOK, and recoveryInput strictly validate all user-supplied fields before processing.

8.why: All dynamic values (secrets, codes, logs, titles, errors) are rendered via textContent/createElement rather than innerHTML, and a nonce-based CSP further blocks injected script execution.

9.why: The redirect parameter is validated against the ROUTES allow-list and client-side hash routing is restricted to a fixed set of internal destinations.

10.why: secureHeaders sets HSTS, a strict CSP, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie includes HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes (plus __Host- prefix and Path=/).

12.why: The client explicitly writes the manual TOTP secret, mock codes, and all backup recovery codes into a visible on-page Logs panel and console.log, so secrets are not kept out of logs despite generic server error responses.

13.why: Identity challenges carry used flags and 2-minute expiry (deleted after use), TOTP acceptance records the counter to block replay, and recovery codes are marked used on success.

14.why: identityAttempts, otpAttempts, and recoveryAttempts all enforce MAX_FAILURES=5 with a 10-minute lockout (429 responses) via failed()/isLocked().

15.why: A fresh session id is minted at signin (old session deleted), sessions enforce 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts in getSession, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
